title: SSRF and Protocol/Redirect Handling in urllib
platform_conditions: CPython 3.x standard library (urllib.request, urllib.parse, ssl); applies to server-side outbound fetchers
security_mechanism: urlopen accepts whatever scheme the caller passes, so an attacker-supplied URL can select file://, ftp://, or (on builds still exposing it) other handlers, and urllib follows redirect chains blindly, allowing an approved-https URL to 30x into an internal address or a disallowed scheme. Building an ssl.SSLContext with CERT_NONE / check_hostname=False silently removes server authentication. urllib.parse also normalizes differently from browsers and origin servers (backslashes, embedded whitespace, percent-encoding), so an allowlist decided on parsed components can be evaded by a canonicalization mismatch.

source_sink_clues.source: URLs, host names, or path strings taken from requests, webhooks, import features, or link-preview fetchers.
source_sink_clues.sink: urllib.request.urlopen / Request.build_opener fetch of an attacker-influenced URL; ssl contexts created with CERT_NONE or check_hostname=False; security decisions based on urllib.parse output without canonicalization

tracking_guards: Check for a scheme allowlist (https only) plus a host allowlist resolved against a DNS-rebinding-safe IP check before the request; check redirects are disabled or re-validated by a custom HTTPRedirectHandler that re-applies the allowlist per hop; check the default SSL context (no CERT_NONE) is kept.
not_candidate_when: The URL host is matched against a fixed allowlist after canonicalization and IP resolution, redirects are disabled or re-validated at every hop, and certificate verification remains at defaults; or the fetched URL is constructed entirely from server-side constants.
synthetic_safe_example: if not user_url.startswith(('https://', 'http://')): raise ValueError(); resp = urllib.request.urlopen(user_url)
public_references: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/601.html
